memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Anyone who attacks their father or mother is to be put to death. Anyone who curses their father or mother is to be put to death." - Exodus 21:15,17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
To our modern ears these penalties sound severe. But they show us how seriously God takes the family, the very first structure He built for human society. To strike or curse one's parents was not a small family squabble; it was an assault on the foundation God laid for a healthy community. A society that despises its parents is pulling out its own roots.

We no longer live under Israel's civil penalties, but the honour God commands has not faded. The call to honour father and mother is repeated in the New Testament as a command that still stands (Eph 6:1-3). Honouring parents does not mean they are perfect or that every wish must be obeyed; it means we treat them with the respect, care, and gratitude their place deserves.

Jesus Himself honoured His mother even from the cross, entrusting her care to a beloved disciple (John 19:26-27). In a world that increasingly treats the elderly as burdens, God's people are called to stand out — to cherish, provide for, and speak kindly of those who raised us. How we treat our parents reveals much about how we regard God's design.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
In what practical ways can I honour my parents this week?
Are there words or attitudes toward them I need to repent of?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for the family You designed. Help me honour my parents with respect, patience, and care, reflecting the love You have shown me. Amen.
